review.summary: Base.one for Complex{Interval} returned complex(one, one), giving an imaginary part of [1,1] instead of [0,0], which violates the multiplicative identity semantics of one. The minimized patch pulls zero and one out of the shared metaprogramming loop so one sets the imaginary component to zero. The isthinone API addition from the same commit is excluded from the trigger and the minimized patch, leaving a single-hunk behavioral fix.
review.evidence: Issue #601 reports one on complex intervals returning [1,1] + im*[1,1] when [1,1] + im*[0,0] is expected; PR #602 closes it. The one-hunk production diff in src/intervals/real_interface.jl replaces the loop-generated Complex methods with explicit zero (both parts zero) and one (real one, imaginary zero) definitions. Trigger test 'one for complex intervals has zero imaginary component' in test/interval_tests/consistency.jl fails on parent 0974c8a and passes on b702da4; strict differential is stable across 3 repetitions and the fixed full suite passes.
review.missing_evidence: The actual test source for the trigger assertion is not shown, only its name. The full commit including isthinone was not provided, so the exclusion of the new API rests on the minimization report rather than direct inspection.
review.validation_risks: Low. The zero definitions are semantically unchanged from the loop expansion, so only one behavior differs; any hidden coupling to the previous incorrect one (e.g. code relying on one for complex identity arrays or promotion) could surface elsewhere, but the passing full suite argues against it. Minor risk that the trigger test file also exercises isthinone and would error on the buggy-plus-minimized-patch combination if the test file is taken wholesale.
review.suggested_tests: Assert one(Complex{Interval{Float64}}) == complex(interval(1), interval(0)) and one(complex(interval(2,3), interval(4,5))) == complex(interval(1), interval(0)); verify z * one(z) == z for several complex intervals; confirm zero(Complex{Interval{Float64}}) still has both parts thin zero; check isguaranteed propagation for both zero and one on complex intervals; test with Float32 and BigFloat NumTypes.

swe.problem_statement:
"one" on complex intervals returns wrong value
Hello,

It seems that in the more recent update the function "one" for complex intervals seems to return [1, 1] + im*[1, 1] (even though I assume that the value we want to get out of this function is [1, 1] + im*[0, 0]).

diff --git a/test/interval_tests/consistency.jl b/test/interval_tests/consistency.jl
index 03ced2d3..30881728 100644
--- a/test/interval_tests/consistency.jl
+++ b/test/interval_tests/consistency.jl
@@ -36,6 +36,14 @@
         @test isequal_interval(a * interval(0), zero(a))
     end
 
+    @testset "real interface" begin
+        @test isthinzero(zero(Interval{Float64}))
+        @test isthinzero(zero(Complex{Interval{Float64}}))
+
+        @test isthinone(one(Interval{Float64}))
+        @test isthinone(one(Complex{Interval{Float64}}))
+    end
+
     @testset "inv" begin
         @test isequal_interval(inv( zero(a) ), emptyinterval())  # Only for set based flavor
         @test isequal_interval(inv( interval(0, 1) ), interval(1, Inf))
